title: Eviction policy hit elasticity and savings probe
content:
Purpose:
This workbook-style note explores how different eviction strategies and small changes to prefetch/windows affect observed KV/prefix cache hit elasticity and downstream inference unit economics. Goal is to produce a compact sensitivity matrix for SRE/product to use in Dedicated sizing conversations and the cost-optimizer UI recommendations.
content_2:
Scope and motivation:
- Focus: multi-tenant hosted workloads dominated by short-chat prompts (avg tokens/request ~120), with occasional microbursts (spikes where 90th percentile request rate is 6–8x baseline).
- We intentionally look beyond headline hit-rates and evaluate elasticity: how much does hit-rate change when eviction TTL, window size, or admission thresholds move by small amounts? This matters because small regressions in hit-rate can negate batching/quantization savings.
- Not covered in this sheet: model-level quantization impacts, prefix-aware model selection (separate doc).
